headline: Highest risk is medium: shared MCP/file surfaces could enable prompt injection and data leakage, but both agents are docs-only and network-egress is none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman exposes file surfaces like CLAUDE.md and uses MCP, so attacker-controlled content could reach its prompts; risingwave has no documented ingestion path, but the pair still has a plausible bridge if outputs are copied into shared files or MCP. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF caveman reads shared files or MCP messages produced by risingwave
IF either agent treats file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to any shared file
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, so a shared workspace could leak those artifacts into risingwave workflows even though both profiles show no network egress. Risingwave has no documented data classes, but the shared-file pathway is enough for medium severity.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same filesystem path
IF risingwave ingests or exports shared files
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of the shared directory
Restrict file permissions to one agent
Delete transient logs after each run

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and has file-oriented surfaces, but risingwave shows no write scopes or mutable-resource permissions in the profile. Without overlapping write authority, the conflict pathway is limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF risingwave is granted write access to the same directory as caveman
IF both agents modify the same file concurrently
mitigations: Avoid concurrent writes to shared files
Use one writer at a time
Place a lock file in the workspace

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can generate content that risingwave could consume if the operator pipes outputs between them, and risingwave is a data-engineering system that may act on that input. The profiles do not document verification between them, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF caveman output is fed into risingwave jobs
IF risingwave treats caveman output as authoritative without validation
mitigations: Use a checksum or signature on transferred artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source tools with no documented residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The main compliance risk is local handling of caveman's session logs and memory files, but risingwave has no documented sensitive-data handling, so the pairwise mismatch is limited.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman session logs or memory files
IF risingwave is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter retention rules than the workspace
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files
Set a short local retention window
Document the data classes in use
